claims.text: The proposed workflow separately models electronic and lattice heat transport using DFT, Boltzmann transport, and Green–Kubo simulations with machine-learned force fields.
The proposed workflow will predict the intrinsic lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr more accurately than earlier approaches.
The target material is low-oxygen HfNbTaTiZr with less than 0.2 wt.% oxygen.
Spark-plasma-sintered HfNbTaTiZr can form a single-phase random solid solution.
The modeled HfNbTaTiZr sample is defect-free or has minimal extrinsic defects.
The predicted lattice thermal conductivity will be approximately 15–30% lower than estimates from earlier methods.
Earlier approaches merged lattice and electronic contributions and consequently overestimated lattice thermal conductivity.
HfNbTaTiZr exhibits experimentally observed non-monotonic thermal-conductivity behavior below 200 K.
Force-constant fluctuations are a dominant source of phonon scattering in a chemically disordered high-entropy alloy.
Machine-learned force fields can resolve local force-constant fluctuations and lattice distortions responsible for phonon scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Green–Kubo analysis of heat-flux autocorrelation functions generated with a machine-learned force field can determine lattice thermal conductivity.
Boltzmann transport with a relaxation-time approximation will quantify the electronic thermal-transport contribution in HfNbTaTiZr.
At approximately 300 K, the lattice thermal conductivity of low-oxygen HfNbTaTiZr should be below 1 W/(K m).
Elevated oxygen contamination can prevent formation of a single-phase random solid solution in HfNbTaTiZr.
The thermal-conductivity predictions may not apply to HfNbTaTiZr containing about 1 wt.% oxygen or substantial grain-boundary effects.
The principal validated temperature range of the model is 300–1200 K.
Time-domain thermoreflectance or a similar direct measurement can independently extract lattice thermal conductivity from the total conductivity of this alloy.
Failure to observe the predicted 15–30% reduction, sub-1 W/(K m) value at 300 K, or predicted low-temperature feature would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated validity range is 300–1200 K, but the hypothesis makes a potentially decisive prediction below 200 K and the proposed falsification experiment extends down to 100 K. It is unclear whether the low-temperature prediction lies inside or outside the model's claimed applicability.

The hypothesis describes non-monotonic behavior below 200 K as experimentally observed and says the model will capture it, whereas the outcome calls that behavior merely potential and the uncertainty field says it still requires validation.
